newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stoiber says does not want to be German chancellor.
newsitem.headline: Stoiber says does not want to be German chancellor.

text.p: Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber said he will not put himself forward as a candidate for the German chancellorship in next year's general election, a newspaper reported on Sunday.
In a release ahead of publication on Monday, Munich's Sueddeutschen Zeitung daily said Stoiber wanted to end the "senseless speculation" about whether he wanted to stand.
Stoiber said he had fulfilled his career goals in his position as premier of the southern state of Bavaria.
Stoiber had been seen as second favourite to succeed Chancellor Helmut Kohl, after Kohl's closest aide Wolfgang Schauble and ahead of Defence Minister Volker Ruehe.
Kohl, who has been in power for 14 years, has promised to decide whether to stand again after a European Union summit in June.
A recent poll in the weekly Der Spiegel said 40 percent of Germans saw Schaeuble as the best conservative successor to Kohl, with 24 percent for Stoiber and 14 percent for Ruehe.

Stoiber's chancellery credentials stemmed from his success in dragging Bavaria's Christian Social Union (CSU), sister party of Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), out of a mire of corruption scandals and shoring up a conservative majority in Germany's biggest state.
He had also played to ordinary German fears of a single currency by making himself the most prominent conservative critic of European monetary union.
